llm.summary: This memory skill is not clearly malicious, but it broadly records, reuses, archives, and can sync conversation history with limited user controls.

dimensions.detail: The default workspace is broad agent memory storage, and the vault sync script can copy archived logs to hard-coded NAS/Tailscale targets using a local SSH key; this is disclosed but high-impact for private conversation data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install flow symlinks local scripts into PATH and relies on shell, file read/write, and network sync behavior, but the skill metadata does not define explicit permission boundaries or scoped capabilities.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to search memory before answering, treat memory files as the source of truth, and auto-log user messages and replies after every interaction without a clear opt-in, no-log mode, or strong redaction requirement.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Daily logs, checkpoints, decision files, fresh recaps, and verbatim PDFs persist plaintext content, preserve historical copies, and can resurface prior text into future sessions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The file writes, search, checkpointing, PDF archive, and NAS sync are coherent with the stated multi-layer agent memory purpose, but the purpose itself involves broad retention of user-agent interactions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want conversation history and operational notes stored in plaintext memory files, summarized into future context, archived as PDFs, and possibly synced to a NAS. Review the hard-coded NAS/SSH settings, add redaction and retention limits, and avoid using it for passwords, tokens, private keys, regulated data, or sensitive personal/business conversations unless you add stronger controls first.
llm.findings:
[TT2] expected: The raw writes to markdown, JSON checkpoints, and recaps are expected for a memory system, but the artifact does not sufficiently separate stored user text from future instructions or sanitize content before replay.
[LP3] expected: Shell and file access are needed for the advertised tools, but the skill lacks explicit capability scoping for local writes, reads, symlinks, environment-controlled workspace paths, and NAS sync.
[TP4] expected: Checkpointing, recap generation, restoration, PDF archiving, and NAS sync are mostly disclosed in SKILL.md and README.md, so this is not hidden behavior; the concern is under-controlled scope rather than tool poisoning.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent logging is central to the skill, but the primary runtime instructions do not require consent before storing conversations or give strong default protections for secrets and sensitive data.
[SSD-3] expected: Long-lived memory and verbatim archives are stated features, but indefinite collection, repeated resurfacing, and optional off-host sync create a real data exposure concern.
[RA2] expected: Session persistence is an intended recovery feature, not evidence of a rogue agent; it remains review-worthy because it automatically carries prior context into later sessions.
